timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm Somia Gopta, I'm in DP1 and I'm from Ambasa.
I'm involved with a couple of different things.
So there's MUN, tennis, there's obviously piano.
I'm organizing a TEDx event in January, I'm in the SRC, so I'm the citizenship exec for
senior school.
I started playing piano pretty late, I started playing piano when I was in grade 3, that
makes me 8 or 9.
But I instantly fell in love with just playing the piano.
During these summer holidays I took part in the Kenya Music Festival, which is a national
music competition and I represented Akam in the piano solo advanced category.
It's basically the family that's at Akam that makes it so special.
The people, obviously the people who come and go, but at the end of the day it's like
you're all like one moving body and you're just like moving forward together.
And the way the school structures its education is so that you start questioning how you
reason and I think that's one of the biggest things that will come out of me being at the
school, which I'm really grateful for.
We have them creating this culture where you're taught that you're even though you're
this young or even though you're this old, you can still make an impact and that's what
matters.
It doesn't matter how big the impact is, but there's always a way to do something.
Being a leader for me is about making an impact.
It's not necessarily about having a following or having an influence over people because I
think being a leader is being able to recognize who you are and how you can change yourself
and how you can make that impact, positive impact obviously on the people surrounding you.
My name is Samin, I'm a leader.
